answer: Work slots stop forgery at the point of work. Each slot locks a 50-credit deposit, and a jury of five spot-checks 10% of slots each epoch, publishing verdicts in an atlas. A slot counts only when its completion signal matches the assigned task; a forged slot burns the deposit, and a rented slot fails because deposit and evidence bind to one worker key. Forging 1,000 slots costs 50,000 credits plus 1,000 forged records, linear with no bulk discount, while an honest agent risks one deposit per slot, recovered on verified work. The audit trail is a canyon wall: past verdicts stay visible.
